title: A Family Bought A $1.3M House. Then Letters From 'The Watcher' Started Arriving.
description:
In 2014, a New Jersey family bought their dream home. Before they even moved in, someone calling themselves The Watcher started sending letters.

#shorts #truestory #unsolvedmystery
sources: Wikipedia's "The Watcher of Westfield, New Jersey" entry
CBS News's account of the real story behind Netflix's The Watcher
NBC News's coverage of the Broaddus family's lawsuit and the house sale

scenes.text: In June of 2014, Derek and Maria Broaddus bought their dream home in Westfield, New Jersey, for one point three million dollars.
Before they even moved in, they got a typed letter. It said the house had been watched by the same family for generations, and called their three young kids 'new blood.'
More letters followed. Whoever was writing them knew the family's names, their car, and details about the renovation work happening inside the house in real time.
The family never moved in. They spent about a hundred thousand dollars trying to fix the house up, then tried to get permission to tear it down instead. The town said no.
scenes.visual_query: empty house for sale sign daytime

scenes.text: They finally sold the house years later, at a loss. Police have said there's never been a confirmed suspect.
The letters stopped. Whoever called themselves The Watcher was never identified, and the case is still officially open.
